newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - May 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - May 21.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.
- Prosecutors seized and searched about 150 bank accounts opened at 10 banks by the jailed second son of President Kim Young-sam and a former intelligence official to trace fund flows.
- Stock prices rallied to this year's highest closing: the composit price index jumped 13.47 points to 734.67, highest since November 28.
- Prosecutors plan to indict seven politicians for accepting bribes from the stricken Hanbo Group.

- In order to inject some life into the dormant provincial economies, and therby achive more balanced development, the government announced a policy package aimed at giving local administrations more say in land, tax and manpower affairs.
- Seoul and Washington opened a two-day meeting to discuss the signing of an 'open skies' agreement, with the U.S. side calling for the lifting of a series of aviation-related restrictions.
